name: Make
tagline: Visual automation platform for scenarios across apps and APIs

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Core listed at $12/month for 10,000 credits.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1,000 credits/month; 2 active scenarios; 15-minute minimum schedule; 5-minute execution cap; 5 MB files.

tiers.name: Core
tiers.limits: 10,000 credits/month at entry price; unlimited active scenarios; 1-minute scheduling; 40-minute runs; 100 MB files.
tiers.notes: Price scales with the selected credit allowance from 10,000 to 8,000,000+ credits/month.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 10,000 credits/month at entry price; unlimited scenarios; priority execution; 250 MB files; 30-day logs.

tiers.name: Teams
tiers.limits: 10,000 credits/month at entry price; unlimited users and scenarios; team roles; 500 MB files; 30-day logs.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom credits; unlimited scenarios; 1,000 MB files; 60-day logs; overage protection.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1,000 credits/month, 2 active scenarios, 15-minute scheduling, 5-minute execution cap and 5 MB maximum file size
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual saves at least 15%); annual credits can remain usable for the 12-month term
pricing.hiddenCosts: Most module actions use 1 credit, but AI and code features can use more. Extra-credit packs or auto-purchase are available; credits expire at the end of the monthly or annual term, and scenarios pause when credits run out unless protection is enabled.

verdictSummary: A handful of workflows can be coded quickly, but Make's paid value is the visual builder, app modules, scheduling, observability, and maintenance.
coreLoopDIY: Implement the needed scenarios as scripts or n8n workflows with API calls, retries, and logs.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because workflows evolve and break; a maintained builder reduces the upkeep.

priorArt.name: Activepieces
priorArt.desc: Open-source automation platform with app pieces, triggers, and actions.

alternatives.name: Activepieces Community Edition
alternatives.desc: A polished visual workflow builder with hundreds of connectors and one Docker command.

facts.install: Run one Docker container for personal/testing use, or Docker Compose with PostgreSQL and Redis for production.
facts.engines: AI pieces connect to providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google Gemini using user-supplied credentials.
facts.dataFormat: Single-container mode stores data under ~/.activepieces; production uses PostgreSQL and Redis, with files/logs optionally in S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Activepieces is less mature for Make-style complex mapping, branching and run inspection, and production use still needs infrastructure.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker; public webhooks need a reachable HTTPS URL, while production also needs PostgreSQL, Redis and managed secrets.

alternatives.name: Automatisch
alternatives.desc: A cleaner, smaller automation canvas when your scenarios do not need Make's long tail.

facts.install: Clone the repository and run Docker Compose.
facts.dataFormat: Application and credential data stays on the user's server in PostgreSQL, with Redis for queues/cache; credentials are encrypted.
facts.gapVsPaid: Automatisch's connector catalog and transformation canvas are far narrower than Make's long-tail scenario system.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker, PostgreSQL/Redis configuration and secret management; the default sample login must be changed immediately.

alternatives.name: n8n Community Edition
alternatives.desc: The closest broad replacement, with more self-hosting and fewer glossy scenario diagrams.

facts.install: Install with Docker or npm; Docker is the recommended production path.
facts.engines: AI nodes connect to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama and many other model/vector backends.
facts.dataFormat: SQLite stores workflows, credentials and executions by default; PostgreSQL is supported, with binary data in the database, filesystem or object storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: n8n is the closest substitute but its workflow UX is more technical and self-hosting replaces Make's managed execution layer.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server, HTTPS and a public webhook URL for many integrations, plus ongoing updates, backups and provider credentials.

notes: Good smaller Zapier comparison; same reasoning but different builder style.
prompt:
Build me a code-first workflow runner to replace Make for my handful of scenarios. Requirements:

- A Node project where each scenario is one file in scenarios/ exporting a trigger
  (cron string or webhook route) and an ordered list of steps, each step an async
  function that receives the previous step's output.
- The runner executes steps in order, retries a failed step 3 times with
  exponential backoff, then halts the run recording the step name and error.
- Every run saved to SQLite (better-sqlite3): scenario, start/end, per-step input
  and output JSON, status. That history is the debugging story, make it good.
- A minimal dashboard on localhost:4880 (Express, server-rendered): scenario list
  with last-run status, click into a run to see each step's payload.
- Webhook triggers land on the same Express app with signature verification
  helpers; cron triggers via node-cron. All credentials in .env.
- Ship two example scenarios: a Stripe payment webhook appends to a Google Sheet
  and sends a Telegram message; an RSS post gets an LLM summary drafted as email.
- Binds to localhost only, single user, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: a visual drag-and-drop builder and an app-module catalog. Scenarios
  are code, that is the point of this build.
- README: how to add a scenario, .env keys, and a note that self-hosted n8n is the
  off-the-shelf fallback if maintaining this stops being fun.
